verdictStatement: Both Codex advisories are properly folded and the substantive half of its SHOULD-FIX is repaired with real precision: the historical COORD pin is labelled, and I confirmed the exact commit it names actually produces the recorded bytes. Everything the dispatch told me to attack on the contract's merits failed against measurement — the DR-118 row is byte-exact at file 08 line 300, file 02 L308-338 is carried byte-exact, the five-area floor is still explicitly illustrative, DR-125 is now an OPEN activation gate rather than a live vocabulary, no per-row number is minted, the slice-1 role list is byte-identical at TypeScript alone, DR-006 parked recipes are held with 'matrix prose can NEVER settle a parked recipe', and D-056 Class B is stated as still ineligible. What withholds acceptance is that the repair reproduced the defect it was fixing, one generation later and in the block built to cure it: reMeasurementAtV2 records COORD as live at d210f103…, and the live file is b9819d6e…. The historical pin beside it is meticulously qualified; the live one carries no qualifier at all.

shouldFix.title: The live COORD pin introduced to repair CODEX-V1-S1 does not itself reproduce, and unlike the historical pin it is unlabelled

measurement.whatTheRecordedValueIs: The state at commit 499c057 (C-D104). The file has since moved at 36949e3 (C-D105), so the pin is one adopted decision behind.
measurement.theAsymmetry: The key is named livePinsNamedPropertyOnly and carries no standing, no measuredAt marker and no commit identity — an unqualified currency assertion. Two fields away, the historical pin is labelled 'HISTORICAL authoring pin. Not the live path digest.' with historicalCommit 2327cf89106e3c58a317bf8b570697f3505dbbb8 and an explanatory note. The artifact demonstrably knows how to qualify a pin and did not qualify this one.
measurement.theOtherLivePinIsFine: The file 08 entry in the same block records 1cdcf9d4… and that does reproduce against live bytes, so only the COORD half is stale.

shouldFix.whatIVerifiedSoThisIsNotWorse: I did not assume the substance survived. The three sections this pin is scoped to — D-002, D-007 and D-056 — I extracted from the historical 2327cf89 blob and from the current live file and compared: all three are byte-identical. So the role list, the acceptance structure, and the Class-B ineligibility claim all still hold at live bytes, and no claim in the contract is affected. That is why this is a SHOULD-FIX and not a blocker.
shouldFix.whyItStillMatters: This is the finding Codex raised at v1, in Codex's own words 'an objective failure of a declared governing-source pin: a reviewer following the recorded path cannot reproduce the recorded bytes or know from the artifact whether the mismatch is intentional history or unnoticed drift'. That sentence now applies to the block created to answer it. The artifact even appends the attack line that catches it — 'Attack a COORD pin at the live path that does not reproduce and is unlabeled' — and its own new live pin fails that test. I note in fairness that d210f103 may well have been current when v2 was authored, since C-D105 landed afterwards; but the field asserts currency without an authoring-time qualifier, which is precisely the distinction the historical pin draws so carefully.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Either re-measure the live COORD pin to b9819d6e… and note C-D105 as the mover, or give the live block the same qualification discipline as the historical one — a measuredAt commit and a standing — so a reader can tell a stale-by-design snapshot from unnoticed drift without leaving the document. Re-verifying the three named sections at whatever bytes are recorded would make the block self-checking.

repairVerification.finding: CODEX-V1-A1 — performance-baseline rows should record runner and environment
repairVerification.detail: rowFields.required gains a ninth member: 'performance-baseline runner and environment (OBS-D007-T2-01). Required when the row carries a performance baseline. Absence is an explicit no-runner-recorded claim, not a default.' That last clause matters — it forecloses silent omission, which is the failure mode the advisory was about. A new baselines.runnerAndEnvironment field restates the D-007 observation and closes with 'It does not mint runner classes or numbers', so the repair adds an obligation without minting a vocabulary. The thresholds section ties the two together: inventing numbers 'would repeat the class D-006's reviewer struck (a threshold whose runner/workload is unnamed measures nothing)'.

repairVerification.finding: CODEX-V1-A2 — the DR-125 dependency should be stated as an open activation gate
repairVerification.detail: matrixShape.capabilityBoundary now adds 'DR-125 is OPEN. That closure is an activation gate for matrix authoring (D-007 OBS-D007-T2-02): this artifact does not treat DR-125 as accepted, does not author a matrix, and does not use DR-125 as a live capability vocabulary', with the scoped-disposition follow rule. Matrix authoring waits on that closure or its disposition.' That is both halves of what the advisory asked for.

attacksAttemptedAndFailed: That the historical commit identity was asserted rather than measured. git show of 2327cf89106e3c58a317bf8b570697f3505dbbb8 hashes to exactly the recorded 12d192f7….
That the stale COORD pin invalidates a substantive claim. The three sections it is scoped to are byte-identical between that snapshot and current live bytes.
That the runner/environment repair smuggled in a runner vocabulary or a number. It adds an obligation and says in terms that it mints neither.
That the DR-125 gate is nominal. It names the closure owner, the divergence owner, and the scoped-disposition follow rule, and denies live-vocabulary use.

That a substantive block drifted while attention was on the pin. Only the eleven rostered top-level keys changed; the carried file-02 text, the register row, the role list and the obligation decomposition are untouched.
That the threshold reservation is weakened anywhere. Every threshold surface reads RESERVED or UNDECIDED, and the artifact gives a reason rather than a hedge.
coordinatorNote: This successor does the hard part well. The historical-pin repair is the strongest form of that fix I have seen in this corpus — it names the exact commit, and that commit really does produce the recorded bytes — and both advisories are folded with obligations rather than gestures, including the useful clause that a missing runner/environment is an explicit claim rather than a default. Every contract-merits attack the dispatch listed failed against measurement. The single SHOULD-FIX is narrow and slightly unlucky: the block created to answer Codex's pin finding introduced a live COORD digest that went stale when C-D105 was adopted, so the artifact now carries a carefully-qualified historical pin beside an unqualified live pin that does not reproduce. I verified the three sections that pin is scoped to are byte-identical between the historical snapshot and live bytes, so nothing substantive is wrong and no claim in the contract is affected — the fix is one re-measure or one label. DR-118 stays DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED, no threshold is minted, and nothing here marks the row SATISFIED or authorizes docs/v2/implementation/.
